This Guide will explain how to access all sets and reps performed for a given team.

# Set up API Token

Below is the code to set up your API Token. Please reference the [Get Started Guide](getting-started.Rmd).

```{r setup, eval = FALSE}
# Load the eliteformR package
library(eliteformR)

token <- EF_CreateAPIToken(Sys.getenv("ELITEFORM_API_KEY"))

# Download Team List
team_list_df <- EF_GetTeamsList(token)

# Update the Token with the Selected Team ID
token <- EF_UpdateTokenTeam(token, team_list_df$id[1])
# or
# token <- EF_UpdateTokenTeam(token, 111)
```

# Get All Sets

`EF_GetAllSets()` returns the completed sets for a team on one workout day, which is the current date if you only include the Token. To specify a date, include the `date` argument as a Date or as a string in any of these formats: "%m/%d/%Y", "%m-%d-%Y", "%m%d%Y", "%Y/%m/%d", "%Y-%m-%d", "%Y%m%d".

To leave out sets entered through Paperless, set `includePaperless` to 0.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Completed sets for the current date, including Paperless
all_sets_df <- EF_GetAllSets(token)

# Completed sets on a date
all_sets_df <- EF_GetAllSets(token, "08/03/2026")

# Only sets tracked at the rack
all_sets_df <- EF_GetAllSets(token, "08/03/2026", includePaperless = 0)
```

A max-reps set has `isMaxReps` TRUE and `repsAssigned` NA, and a bodyweight set has `isBodyweight` TRUE and `loadFactor` NA. Totals and averages over those columns can skip the NAs with `na.rm = TRUE`.

## Filters and ranges

Any other filter the API offers can be passed by name. To read a range of days, use `dateAfter` and `dateBefore` instead of `date`. `dateBefore` is exclusive, and a range can span at most 366 days. One call over a range uses far fewer requests than one call per day.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# All of August for two athletes
august_df <- EF_GetAllSets(token, dateAfter = "2026-08-01", dateBefore = "2026-09-01", athleteId = c(6, 13))

# One exercise
bench_df <- EF_GetAllSets(token, "08/03/2026", exerciseId = 88)

# Sets on the card that have not been done yet
planned_df <- EF_GetAllSets(token, "08/03/2026", hasResults = FALSE)

# Every set, done or not
every_set_df <- EF_GetAllSets(token, "08/03/2026", hasResults = NULL)
```

## The reps of a set

Each tracked set carries its own reps in the `reps` column, as a data frame. A Paperless set has a data frame with no rows.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
all_sets_df$reps[[2]][, c("repNumber", "avgVelocity", "peakVelocity", "avgPower")]

#   repNumber avgVelocity peakVelocity avgPower
# 1         1        0.62         0.95    410.3
# 2         2        0.58         0.90    395.0
```

## Targets

When the workout prescribes a velocity, power or work target, the set carries it in `targetMetric`, `targetBasis`, `targetMin` and `targetMax`. `targetMetric` names the rep column the target applies to, and `targetBasis` says whether the numbers are `absolute` or a fraction of one of the athlete's bests. All four are NA when no target was prescribed.

# Get All Reps

`EF_GetAllTrackedReps()` returns one row per rep tracked at the rack, with the set's context on every row. It takes the same `date` and filters as `EF_GetAllSets()`, plus `setId`. Paperless sets have no reps. Use `EF_GetAllSets()` for those.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Defaults to the current date
all_reps_df <- EF_GetAllTrackedReps(token)
all_reps_df <- EF_GetAllTrackedReps(token, date = "08/03/2026")

all_reps_df[, c("setId", "athleteId", "exerciseId", "repNumber", "avgVelocity", "peakPower")]

#    setId athleteId exerciseId repNumber avgVelocity peakPower
# 1 918224         6         88         1        0.62     620.8
# 2 918224         6         88         2        0.58     600.2
```

The eccentric columns (`eccentricAvgVelocity` and so on) are NA when the rack did not record the lowering phase.

Reps do not carry the set's weight or rest. To add them, join on the set:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
sets_df <- EF_GetAllSets(token, "08/03/2026")
reps_with_load_df <- merge(all_reps_df, sets_df[, c("id", "actualWeight", "loadFactor", "actualRest")],
                           by.x = "setId", by.y = "id")
```

`EF_GetAllTrackedReps3()` is deprecated and returns the same as `EF_GetAllTrackedReps()`.
